presentation_meta.title: Turning Meetings into Instant Enterprise-Grade Artifacts
presentation_meta.subtitle: AI inside Teams that converts spoken intent into PPT/Docs and makes Copilot indispensable
presentation_meta.focus: Secure resources to build a doc co-creation agent in Teams that transforms meetings into real-time, high-quality PPT/Word artifacts, deepening Teams’ role as the OS of work and driving Copilot monetization.
presentation_meta.scqa_design: Slide 1: Cover (Answer-first vision). Slides 2–3: Situation & Complication (current meeting-to-document productivity gap, business impact). Slide 4: Question (strategic choice: how to turn Teams into the OS of work and monetize Copilot via doc creation). Slides 5–8: Answer (solution concept, workflow, differentiation, business value, feasibility). Slides 9–10: Commit (resourcing ask, risks, next steps, FAQ alignment).

slides.headline: Turning Meetings into Instant Enterprise-Grade Artifacts
slides.subtitle: AI inside Teams that converts spoken intent into PPT/Docs and makes Copilot indispensable
slides.visual_hint: Simple title layout with a concise before→after tagline and a small three-step flow (Meeting → AI Agent → PPT/Docs) as a framing device.

slides.headline: Manual meeting-to-document workflows waste massive knowledge worker time
slides.subtitle: High-value decisions in meetings still require low-value manual translation into PPT, specs, and work items
slides.speaker_intent: Align that the current way we turn meetings into artifacts is slow, manual, and strategically suboptimal.

sections.title: Meetings drive decisions, but outputs remain largely manual

bullets.text: Modern knowledge work runs on artifacts—PPT decks, Word specs, ADO items—not on raw conversations.
After critical meetings, PMs and leaders still manually translate discussions into specs, slide decks, and work items.
Employees spend disproportionate hours on formatting, layout, and narrative structuring instead of strategic thinking.

sections.title: Document creation volume and expectations are exploding

bullets.text: 30M PPT files are created per day, underscoring how central slides are to enterprise communication.
The rise of tools like Gamma (70M+ users) shows strong demand for AI-assisted content creation at scale.

citation.location: Gamma app has more than 70M users

slides.visual_hint: 2-column layout: left = current workflow funnel (Meetings → Notes → Manual PPT/Docs); right = quantitative callouts (30M PPT/day, 70M Gamma users).

slides.headline: The human bottleneck creates a costly productivity and value gap
slides.subtitle: We lose speed, quality, and Copilot value when humans must manually operate tools after meetings
slides.speaker_intent: Create urgency that the status quo is not just inefficient but a strategic loss of value and competitiveness.

sections.title: Human bottleneck between discussion and artifacts

bullets.text: Participants cannot both follow complex discussions and operate software fast enough to produce structured outputs in real time.
In-meeting discussion and document creation are two separate workflows, causing delays and rework.
The "blank page" problem and lack of design skills make storytelling and polished PPT creation mentally exhausting and slow.
Manual workflows delay execution after decisions are made, reducing the effective speed of the organization.
If AI-assisted content creation shifts to third-party tools, we lose data gravity and weaken Teams’ position as the OS of work.
Competing AI platforms (e.g., Gemini) are racing to own meeting-derived artifacts, eroding our differentiation if we do not act.

slides.visual_hint: Simple loss funnel or leakage chart showing: Meetings → (Human bottleneck) → Delayed / lower-quality artifacts → Lost productivity & weaker ecosystem.

slides.headline: We must turn Teams into the place where meetings become artifacts
slides.subtitle: Key question: How do we convert spoken intent into tool-ready PPT/Docs inside Teams to deepen our moat and monetize Copilot?
slides.speaker_intent: Frame the strategic decision: invest to make Teams the default hub for AI-driven doc creation, or risk ceding that role.

bullets.text: How do we close the productivity gap between live meetings and the creation of enterprise-ready PPT/Word artifacts?
How do we leverage Teams’ unique access to multi-modal meeting data to deliver a differentiated AI experience competitors cannot match?
How do we make Copilot a “must-have” by solving one of the most painful, high-frequency tasks: creating great PPT from discussions?
If the best way to draft a document is to have a meeting in Teams, Teams becomes the OS of work.

slides.visual_hint: Decision question slide with a central question box and three surrounding objectives (Close productivity gap, Leverage Teams data, Monetize Copilot).

slides.headline: AI doc co-creation in Teams converts spoken intent into PPT/Docs
slides.subtitle: A Teams-native agent that generates and co-edits PPT/Word from meetings, chats, and shared content
slides.speaker_intent: Introduce the solution clearly and concretely, linking it directly to the earlier question.

bullets.text: A doc co-creation agent inside Teams that generates PPT and Word documents based on meeting audio/video, chats, shared files, and channel context.

citation.location: What: Develop a doc co-creation agent in Teams

bullets.text: The agent operates during and after meetings, turning live discussion into structured artifacts: specs, slide decks, and ADO items.
Users collaboratively review and edit outputs inside Teams, unifying discussion and document workflows in a single app.

citation.location: enabling Teams users to collaboratively create, review, and edit docs

bullets.text: AI listens to evolving conversations, understands intent, and generates structured content as the meeting unfolds.

citation.location: By enabling AI to do both—understand the evolving conversation and produce structured artifacts

bullets.text: Outputs include updated ADO items, presentation-ready slides, and detailed specifications without manual rework.

citation.location: In a scrum meeting, ADO items could be updated automatically

bullets.text: The content generation engine is extensible to other Microsoft surfaces such as SharePoint and additional content platforms.

citation.location: The content generation engine can also be extended

slides.visual_hint: High-level flow diagram: Inputs (Meetings, Chats, Files, History) → Teams Doc Co-creation Agent → Outputs (PPT, Word, ADO items, Smart Docs).

slides.headline: PPT Maker in Teams eliminates blank pages and design pain
slides.subtitle: A Teams-integrated experience that generates, previews, and refines high-quality slides collaboratively
slides.speaker_intent: Show how the user experience directly addresses the most painful aspects of PPT creation and storytelling.

bullets.text: A "PPT Maker" panel inside Teams provides a conversational interface to request, refine, and guide slide generation.
A live preview window lets users review slides (e.g., advanced AI system overviews) while still in the meeting context.

citation.location: A Preview window where users can review slides

bullets.text: Controls for navigation, thumbnails, and full-screen mode support quick iteration and alignment with stakeholders.

citation.location: Controls for navigation, thumbnails, and full-screen mode

sections.title: Direct relief of user pain points

bullets.text: Automated slide structure and narration reduces the cognitive load of starting from a blank page.
Built-in layout and style assembly produces polished, enterprise-ready designs for users who are not designers.
Co-creation inside the meeting compresses the cycle from discussion to executive-ready slides from days to minutes.

citation.location: In-meeting discussions and doc creation are currently two separate workflows

slides.visual_hint: Storyboard-style layout: left = Teams meeting with PPT Maker side panel; right = fast iteration loop (Prompt → Preview → Approve).

slides.headline: Robust orchestration pipeline makes high-quality artifacts feasible
slides.subtitle: Dispatcher, Miner, Weaver, Structurer, and Assembler collaborate to turn enterprise data into PPTX/DOCX/HTML/MP4
slides.speaker_intent: Demonstrate technical feasibility and thoughtfulness of the architecture to de-risk concerns about quality and buildability.

bullets.text: Orchestrator with a Dispatcher plans tasks based on user input, meeting context, and desired outputs (slides, chapters, instructions).
Miner component extracts facts from enterprise data (meetings, chats, docs) into a structured content pool of atoms (architecture, metrics, code, etc.).
Weaver generates coherent narration, while Structurer organizes content into slides and chapters tailored to the audience.

citation.location: Content Creation: A Weaver handles narration, while a Structurer organizes slides and chapters

bullets.text: Assembler manages layout and style and uses an engine (HTML, FFMPEG, python-pptx) to render final artifacts (HTML, PPTX, DOCX, MP4).

citation.location: Final Output: An Assembler manages layout and style

bullets.text: Clear separation of concerns (mining, weaving, structuring, assembling) enables iterative improvement of each stage, including aesthetic evaluation.
Engine supports multiple output formats, enabling reuse of the same content pipeline across PPT, Word, HTML, and video.
Architecture is compatible with extension to other Microsoft apps such as SharePoint and broader content platforms.

citation.location: content generation engine can also be extended

slides.visual_hint: Process flow / value chain diagram: Dispatcher → Miner → Content Pool → Weaver → Structurer → Assembler → Engine → Artifacts (consulting-style process chart).

slides.headline: Teams’ data, ecosystem, and Office formats give us a durable moat
slides.subtitle: Only Microsoft can combine meeting data, file standards, and Copilot to deliver seamless, editable artifacts
slides.speaker_intent: Convince leadership that this is a strategically advantaged bet for Microsoft and hard for competitors to copy.

bullets.text: Microsoft owns the full stack: meeting data (Teams), file standards (PPTX/DOCX), and AI (Copilot), enabling deep integration.
Competitors can summarize meetings, but cannot natively generate high-fidelity, editable Office documents as seamlessly.
Teams’ multi-modal grounding (audio/video, chats, shared files, histories) allows richer context than standalone PPT agents.

sections.title: Business value flywheel for Teams and Copilot

bullets.text: "One-click to PPT" becomes a killer Copilot feature that directly supports the $30/month license value proposition.

citation.location: The 'Killer App' for AI: 'One-click to PPT'

bullets.text: By moving doc creation inside Teams, we increase time-in-app and position Teams as the OS of work, boosting retention.
The more users rely on Teams to create artifacts, the more data and workflows stay in our ecosystem, reinforcing data gravity.

slides.visual_hint: Flywheel diagram: Teams usage ↑ → More meetings & data → Better AI artifacts → More doc creation in Teams → Stronger Copilot value → Teams usage ↑.

slides.headline: Focused investment unlocks WOW quality and mitigates key risks
slides.subtitle: Targeted dev and design resources address technical, aesthetic, and narrative challenges
slides.speaker_intent: Show that we understand the risks and have a clear plan to address them with specific resourcing.

sections.title: Key challenges to delivering a WOW experience

bullets.text: Achieving truly impressive slide quality requires robust aesthetic evaluation and style control, not just basic generation.

citation.location: Technical: To achieve a 'WOW' effect is difficult. Aethetic Eval

bullets.text: Systematic narrative generation is needed to ensure coherent, executive-ready storylines rather than disconnected bullets.
Dataset building for layout, style, and narrative evaluation is non-trivial and requires dedicated focus.
Current SOX CMD resources are insufficient to own and drive this project end-to-end.
Secure 6 developers (including at least 3 senior engineers) to build and harden the orchestration pipeline and integrations.
Add dedicated designer resources to define aesthetic evaluation metrics and ensure enterprise-grade visual quality.

citation.location: Designer resource, important for defining Eval metrics

bullets.text: Leverage or integrate with existing services (e.g., Societas) where ready, to accelerate time-to-value and reduce duplication.

citation.location: We are open to integrate with any services

slides.visual_hint: Risk→Mitigation matrix (Harvey Balls or 2-column table): rows for WOW quality, narrative, dataset, ownership; columns for Risk / Mitigation / Owner.
